workflow: Multiple isolated execution contexts share objects or internal references created under a legacy initialization model.
One context shuts down and frees context-owned bookkeeping or shared values without accounting for references retained by another context.
The surviving context retains links or values whose backing storage belongs to the released context.
Later use or cleanup follows those stale references, causing invalid memory access and process termination instead of safe teardown.
summary: Cross-context shared state outlives its owner
